children: Hotels and resorts are seeing a sharp rise in wedding enquiries and advance bookings, with key destinations reporting strong demand for the January–March 2027 season

Hotels and resorts across India are witnessing a surge in enquiries and advance bookings ahead of the upcoming wedding season, with several properties reporting that prime dates at key destinations are already filling up.

Hoteliers are seeing bookings for the January–March 2027 period coming in four to six months ahead of the season. The trend is being attributed to growing interest in hosting weddings within India, along with increasing domestic travel. Industry players are consequently expecting double-digit revenue growth from the wedding segment in 2027.
Destination weddings and social celebrations that may previously have been hosted overseas are increasingly being brought back to Indian destinations, according to an ITC Hotels spokesperson.

“There is definitely a growing interest in celebrations at home,” the spokesperson says, adding that ITC properties in Udaipur, Kolkata, Goa, Jaipur, Chennai and Gurugram are seeing strong guest interest.
The trend is also visible in Rajasthan, traditionally one of India's prominent wedding destinations.

Anupam Dasgupta, Senior VP, Operations (North India) and Head, Wellness, Leela Palaces Hotels & Resorts, says advance wedding bookings for properties in Jaipur and Udaipur are trending ahead of the levels recorded in 2025.
Hilton Sees Strong Wedding Revenue Pipeline

Hilton is also reporting a significant increase in advance wedding demand. According to Manish Tolani, VP and Commercial Director, South Asia, Hilton, the company's wedding revenue pipeline for 2027 is currently over 50 per cent ahead of where it stood at the same time last year.

“We are also seeing healthy demand across city weddings and increasingly across tier two markets as well. Our recent opening of Hilton Garden Inn in Jabalpur is one example of how this opportunity is broadening geographically,” Tolani says.
The growing demand across both established wedding destinations and emerging markets indicates that India's wedding hospitality opportunity is expanding beyond traditional destination hubs.

With couples and families planning celebrations further in advance, hotels are benefiting from greater visibility into upcoming demand while properties across cities, leisure destinations and tier-two markets compete for a larger share of the wedding business.
